supporter.permittedPattern: {organisation} holds a {lane} Entitlement of the Purpose Source Network; Purpose Fee amount: {amount}; period: {period}; categories: {categories}. verify only at purposesource.org/verify
permittedNotes: Every placeholder is substituted from the certificate the claim is about, never from a marketing document: {organisation} is the subject exactly as the certificate prints it, {lane} is the Entitlement lane it records, {amount} is the Purpose Fee as settled, {period} is the period covered, and {categories} is the published category set.
The payment is the Purpose Fee. It is never described as a contribution or a donation, and the payer is never described as a donor.
The optional clause may state the revenue band the certificate prints. The band is the payer's own self-certification, and that is what the certificate records it as.

The permitted wording is what the certificate records and nothing beyond it. No figure or claim about impact may be added — no outcome, no beneficiary count, no proportion of anything: none exists before a disbursed row of the published ledger.
The closing sentence is reproduced exactly as it stands above, in a claim as on the certificate. No other verification address may be offered beside it.

This version publishes no donation-lane variant. The donate-direct lane is not operable at this phase, so a kit for it would govern claims nobody can make; a later kit version adds one when the lane exists.

The corporate classes this variant does not list — the gift-funder, waived-funder and donation variants of the payment class, and the top-up class — cannot be issued at this phase, so this version states no pattern for them.
prohibited: describing the Purpose Fee as a donation or the organisation as a donor
any verification address other than the one printed on the certificate
supporter.binding: public claims about this certificate are governed by the enclosed claim-language kit

statusOnly.permittedPattern: {organisation} is a Purpose Source Licensed Organization — waiver; coverage status: {status}. verify only at purposesource.org/verify
permittedNotes: Coverage-status wording exclusively. A status certificate attests a recorded status and no payment, so this variant permits no amount, no revenue band, no supporter designation, and no supporter or impact phrasing anywhere.

This version states a pattern for the waiver variant only. The under-threshold and gifted-pass variants of the status class carry their own designations, which the published certificate policy records; neither has been recorded for any organisation at this phase, and a later kit version states their patterns when the surfaces that record them exist.

{organisation} is the subject exactly as the certificate prints it; the designation is reproduced as the published certificate policy records it; and {status} is the coverage status the verify record carries when the claim is made, copied from that record rather than paraphrased.

An organisation covered by a waiver funded nothing. A claim implying that it did would be false rather than merely vague, which is why this variant stands apart from the supporter one instead of narrowing it.
The closing sentence is reproduced exactly as it stands above, in a claim as on the certificate. No other verification address may be offered beside it.
prohibited: describing the Purpose Fee as a donation or the organisation as a donor
any verification address other than the one printed on the certificate
statusOnly.binding: public claims about this certificate are governed by the enclosed claim-language kit

translationsNote: Empty at this phase, and that is a fact rather than a gap: a rendering nobody has approved would be a builder's own translation of a legal constraint. Counsel-approved German and French renderings ship at P-M3, each marked as an approved rendering; the English text of this document is controlling in every case.
